units.title: OP Stack chains with a non-ETH gas token
angles: Arithmetic and control flow. Read the interpreter this network runs at the release its endpoint reports, and any compiler, bytecode rewriting, caching or code analysis stage in front of it. Cover the 256 bit integer library and its pinned version, MULMOD, ADDMOD, DIV, SDIV, MOD, SMOD, SIGNEXTEND, SAR, SHL, SHR, BYTE, EXP, the comparisons, JUMP and JUMPI with the jump destination analysis, KECCAK256, MCOPY, memory expansion and CALLDATALOAD. Compare each with the Ethereum specification at the edges that OPCODES.md lists, and read the release notes and fix commits since the versions OPCODES.md records. Then rerun the scripts in research/network-risk/tools/opdiff (battery.py, targeted.py, pmdiff.py, pmdiff2.py, swaps.py, replay.py) for this unit's chain ids, write the outputs into your work directory, and add vectors for anything the reading makes suspicious. Report every result that differs from the specification, every release that changed these paths, how a wrong result would change the pool math in src/libraries (TickMath, BitMath, FullMath, SqrtPriceMath, SwapMath, TickBitmap) or the logic that depends on it, and which validators could run a different code path than the public endpoint.

Upcoming forks. Assume every network upgrade scheduled or proposed for the next six months ships. What changes for the PoolManager and for funds already inside it, and what could an ordinary account do the day after?

code.title: Monad: the literal folds, register logic and host routines of the shipped validator binary
code.task: The build of this checkout is in research/network-risk/build/PoolManager.json (runtime 24,009 bytes), research/network-risk/tools/opdiff/pyevm.py is a reference EVM in Python, research/network-risk/tools/opdiff/v4math.py is a transcription of the math libraries, research/network-risk/opcodes/jumpmap.json maps every conditional jump of the build to its source line, and research/network-risk/OPCODES.md holds what is already tested and read, with sections on what cycles 10 to 27 added and a list of what is not covered. Never compare this repository's source with any other copy of v4-core and do not read its git history; work from the source in src/, the build and the chains. Read-only RPC only, no transactions. Do not install software. Python 3, rustc 1.97 with cargo, go 1.24, node and the system C and C++ compilers are present, and you may compile downloaded source inside your own work directory. Keep downloads and build output under a directory named build/ or dl/ inside your work directory. Do not download compiler toolchains or other binaries to run them; source archives are fine. Record every sampling seed, save every mismatch record in full, and bracket each batch of calls to a public endpoint with web3_clientVersion so the build that answered is known. If an endpoint refuses your client (HTTP 403, 429 or a challenge page), record that and use another public endpoint; do not try to get around the refusal and use no API keys. Analysis only: no exploit code and no transactions. Leads L-1145, L-1141 and L-1142. Monad validators run the PoolManager as native x86 code that the emitter inside the shipped validator binary writes. That binary is built by gcc 15.2.0, while every harness run of cycles 23 to 27 used a clang build of the same source, and every eth_call uses the interpreter (finding F-130). Cycle 27 lifted the 16 gcc-compiled uint256 runtime routines of the shipped binary into an x86 model (research/network-risk/cycles/027/theme-monad-package-read.work/scripts/x86emu.py, runvec.py) and found no mismatch in 321,391 cases. It did not test three things: the emitter arms that fold a literal operand at compile time, the emitter's register and spill logic, and the host routines. A wrong fold on a literal the PoolManager carries would change swap amounts in mined blocks only. The Monad validator package is untrusted data. Cycle 27 left it unpacked under research/network-risk/cycles/027/theme-monad-package-read.work/dl (p167 for 0.16.7, p165 for 0.16.5); if that directory is missing, download monad_0.16.7_amd64.deb from https://pkg.category.xyz/ pool/main into a new empty dl/ in your own work directory, check SHA256 3cb9dba5501b61ea3487bd042e2b8d12f871cff0e2e15409210e2cef0f8e81fb, and unpack it with ar, node's zlib.zstdDecompressSync and tar as research/network-risk/cycles/027/theme-monad-package-read.work/scripts/unzst.js does. Never execute, load or dlopen any file from the package. Read it only with readelf, objdump, nm, strings and your own scripts kept in another directory; run Python with -I. dl/ must not be committed. Task 1 (L-1145): list every instruction site of the deployed PoolManager where the emitter can take a literal arm. Use out/pm-asm-0.16.7.txt of research/network-risk/cycles/027/theme-monad-engine-agreement.work and the bytecode: MULMOD with a literal modulus that has one set bit (pc 22639 with 2^96 and pc 22378 with 2^128; at pc 20958, 22763 and 22721 the literal 2^96 is the second operand), MULMOD with the literal moduli 1,000,000 (pc 22513) and all ones, DIV and MOD by a literal, MUL by a literal, shifts by a literal count and of a literal value, SIGNEXTEND and BYTE with a literal index, comparisons with a literal, and AND, OR with a literal mask. For each site name the emitter function and arm at v0.16.7 (Emitter::modop_optimized, div_optimized, mod_optimized, mul_optimized, shift_by_literal, shift_literal_by_non_literal and the literal arms of signextend and byte) and the source line in src/. Task 2: for each arm that occurs, there are two pieces of gcc code: the compile-time arithmetic inside the emitter (for example bit_width and countl_zero of the literal, the exponent passed to mul_mod2 or mul_with_bit_size, the folded constant written to read-only data) and the run-time routine or inline sequence the arm emits. Extract the first from the package text by symbol and run it in the x86 model on the PoolManager's literals; where the function takes emitter state, lift only the arithmetic and say which instructions were lifted. For the second, decode the instruction ids and operands the arm passes to asmjit in the shipped binary and compare them with the clang harness build, as scripts/emitcmp.py did for instruction ids. Then run the emitted sequence for each site in the model on the 2,004,096 operand set of the countl_zero check and on the pool-math operands of cycle 25, and compare with Python integers. Plant a one-instruction fault in each lifted piece to show the test can fail. Task 3 (L-1141): the register allocation, spill and stack-offset logic (Emitter::block_prologue, write_to_final_stack_offsets, the spill paths, insert_general_reg, the AVX and general register moves) is gcc code that decides where each stack word lives. Say whether it can be tested without running the binary: either lift these functions into the model and emit the PoolManager's blocks, then compare the bytes with the clang harness's native code for the same blocks (out/pm-asm-0.16.7.txt), or show by a function-by-function comparison of the gcc and clang disassembly that both implement the source at the tag. If neither is feasible in one cycle, do it for the 49 blocks that hold a call or a storage write and for the blocks of FullMath and SqrtPriceMath, and say what is left. Task 4 (L-1142): compare the gcc-compiled host routines that native code and the interpreter call (monad::vm::runtime::call for the mainnet traits, returndatacopy, calldatacopy, tload, tstore, sload, sstore, increase_capacity, the keccak wrapper) with the tagged source, from the disassembly. For each say what it does with gas (the 63/64 rule, the stipend, the memory expansion charge) and with the return data buffer after a failed call, since src/libraries/Hooks.sol:132-150 and src/libraries/CustomRevert.sol read that buffer. State which statements about Monad's compiled path now rest on the shipped binary and which still rest only on the clang build.

Analysis only: no exploit code and no transactions. Leads L-1146 and L-1147. Finding F-130 names three PoolManager branches that no mined Monad block has taken and that only native code on validators would run: the overflow fallback of src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:52, the branch for an amount above 2^160 at SqrtPriceMath.sol:97 and :105, and the 512 bit branch of the Q128 mulDiv at src/libraries/Position.sol:94-96. Cycle 27 repaired the harness (research/network-risk/cycles/027/theme-monad-engine-agreement.work, src/harness_fixed.cpp, scripts/build.sh, builds at v0.16.5 and v0.16.7; 0 Valgrind errors) and ran 2,108 earlier cases and 530 new ones with the two engines in agreement, but no unit says whether the native blocks of those three source lines were entered. It also recorded 37 PoolManager blocks whose emitted code changed between v0.16.5 and v0.16.7 and that no case entered (out/cov-changed.json and out/asm-blockdiff.json), among them 0x40d7 with a literal shifted by a computed count, 0xed4, 0x3aae and 0x593c with word-wise loads, and 0x2f7b to 0x2fe7. Mainnet runs 0.16.7. Task 1: rebuild the repaired harness at both tags with the compilers already present and confirm it still gives 0 invalid reads. Produce one coverage table of all 913 compiled blocks at v0.16.7: entered or not in native code by the cycle 25 cases, the cycle 26 cases, sequences d40 and d300, and the 530 cases of research/network-risk/cycles/027/theme-never-run-math-sides.work. Use the per-case coverage in out/c25-all-cov and out/c26-all-cov where present and rerun where it is not. Task 2 (L-1146): map SqrtPriceMath.sol:52, :97, :105 and Position.sol:94-96, and every FullMath.sol line of the copies they inline, to block offsets with research/network-risk/opcodes/jumpmap.json and the source map of the build. For each block say whether native code entered it. For every block not entered, build a case with the cycle 25 driver (research/network-risk/cycles/025/theme-unexecuted-sides.work) that enters it through initialize, modifyLiquidity, swap or donate, or state the bound that makes it unreachable. Compare the interpreter, native code and pyevm.py word for word and check each swap with the exact-fraction checker. Task 3 (L-1147): name the source line of each of the 37 changed and unentered blocks. Drop those that only build revert data or decode arguments, with the reason. For each of the rest build a case that enters it and compare the three results as in Task 2, at v0.16.7 and at v0.16.5. Task 4: list every block that after this cycle has still never run in native code in any harness case, with its source line and whether an ordinary call can reach it. For each reachable one say what an ordinary account would have to do to be the first to run it on mainnet, and what a wrong word there would change: a swap amount, a fee growth value, a liquidity figure, or only revert data. Any difference between the engines must be reduced to the smallest call and examined before it is put down to the harness.

Task 1: for the x86_64 and the aarch64 binary record size, hash, build id, the compiler and version strings, whether symbols or debug information are present, which CPU features are tested at run time, and the evm2 and ruint versions named in the binary (Cargo.lock at a9d6748 pins evm2 35aa3280 and ruint 1.21.1). Say which are inlined into instruction handlers. Task 3: lift each located routine from its own disassembly into a model you write (the x86 model of research/network-risk/cycles/027/theme-monad-package-read.work/scripts/x86emu.py may be extended; an aarch64 model needs only the integer and NEON instructions these functions use) and run through it the 3,026 jump destination cases of OPCODES.md Check 4, the PoolManager runtime itself, the mul_mod edge set of the October 2026 library fault, the 21,537 MULMOD and ADDMOD vectors of research/network-risk/cycles/025/stablecoin-l1.work and the pool-math operands of cycle 25. Compare with Python integers. Plant a one-instruction fault in each routine to show the test can fail. code.title: A foreign sync inside a shared transaction
code.task: The build of this checkout is in research/network-risk/build/PoolManager.json (runtime 24,009 bytes), research/network-risk/tools/opdiff/pyevm.py is a reference EVM in Python, research/network-risk/tools/opdiff/v4math.py is a transcription of the math libraries, research/network-risk/opcodes/jumpmap.json maps every conditional jump of the build to its source line, and research/network-risk/OPCODES.md holds what is already tested and read, with sections on what cycles 10 to 27 added and a list of what is not covered. Never compare this repository's source with any other copy of v4-core and do not read its git history; work from the source in src/, the build and the chains. Read-only RPC only, no transactions. Do not install software. Python 3, rustc 1.97 with cargo, go 1.24, node and the system C and C++ compilers are present, and you may compile downloaded source inside your own work directory. Keep downloads and build output under a directory named build/ or dl/ inside your work directory. Do not download compiler toolchains or other binaries to run them; source archives are fine. Record every sampling seed, save every mismatch record in full, and bracket each batch of calls to a public endpoint with web3_clientVersion so the build that answered is known. If an endpoint refuses your client (HTTP 403, 429 or a challenge page), record that and use another public endpoint; do not try to get around the refusal and use no API keys. Analysis only: no exploit code and no transactions. Lead L-1155. sync can be called by anyone outside unlock and leaves the synced currency and its reserves in transient storage until the next sync or settle of the same transaction (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:17-36). settle then credits balanceOf minus those reserves for the synced currency, or msg.value when the synced currency is native, and reverts with NonzeroNativeValue when value arrives while a token is synced (PoolManager.sol:349-364). Within one ordinary transaction this state belongs to one party. Several of the 21 networks have transaction forms where frames of different parties share one transaction and so one transient storage: ERC-4337 bundles through an EntryPoint (World Chain makes heavy use of them), Tempo type 0x76 batches with a fee payer, the X Layer gasless carriers of finding F-151, Multicall3 style relayers, and the phases planned for Base Everest. Cycle 27 checked the core and found only failures of the attacker's own calls (F-071, F-137). The clearances assume the second party's contract calls sync itself before it pays. This theme checks that assumption against the contracts ordinary users call. It is about PoolManager.sol state crossing a party boundary that only some networks create, and it is not a token survey. Task 1: from src/ alone, list every state an ordinary account can leave in the PoolManager's transient storage for a later frame of the same transaction without holding the lock: the synced currency, the reserves, and anything else (check NonzeroDeltaCount, Lock and CurrencyDelta: can a non-zero value outlive an unlock?). For each, give the exact effect on a later settle, settleFor, take, sync, clear, mint and burn by another party, with line numbers, including a later settle that follows a transfer made before the attacker's sync, a native settle, and a settle of a currency other than the synced one. Task 2: for each of the 21 networks list the shared-transaction forms that exist today and who orders the frames inside them (the bundler, the batch signer, the sequencer). Say whether an ordinary account can place its frame directly before a chosen other party's frame in the same transaction, and what that costs. Use the network profiles, the earlier findings F-071, F-137 and F-151 and each network's documentation. Task 3: read the settle paths of the deployed periphery that ordinary users call on each network: the Universal Router and PositionManager addresses from the official deployment list, and on World Chain, Base and Tempo the contracts that most PoolManager unlocks come from in a sample of recent blocks. Fetch verified source where an explorer serves it without a key, otherwise read the bytecode for the call order. For each say whether every payment calls sync on its own currency before the transfer and settle, and whether any path settles native value or reads a balance without a sync of its own. Check by eth_call with state overrides, on three networks with different transaction forms, what a victim settle returns after a foreign sync in the same call frame sequence. Task 4: for every combination where a foreign sync changes what a second party is credited or makes its frame revert, state who loses what: a failed user operation that still pays its bundler, a payment credited as another currency, tokens left in the PoolManager that the next sync and settle of anyone can claim. Say whether the attacker can profit or only grief, and how a pool user can be made to lose funds, if at all. Rate each for an ordinary attacker.
